title: A False Dawn
subtitle: Only the dead have seen the end of war.

trails.title: Amid the Chaos
trails.description: Can you hear it? The low hum that comes before a great change.

content.text: A Recent Report on Manus Vindictae​​

Reports continue to arrive from across the globe concerning arcanists operating under Manus Vindictae (a complete list of names and locations can be found in the attached appendix). These individuals have been gathering in coordinated cells, their training evident. Given the efficiency and precision of their attacks against human military forces, it is no longer accurate to call them merely an "organization"; they are, in effect, an army.

Each morning I open what feels like ten thousand urgent messages clamoring for my attention, with still more pleas for reinforcements. Our office has been working without pause. Fatigue has dulled even my anger; nothing surprises me anymore—not even reports of skirmishes between warlords in the eastern territories. At times, I am tempted to reply that they needn't fret; east or west, it makes little difference. The entire world is sliding into chaos.

...

The contingency plan drafted by Creius has now been submitted to the committee for review. It addresses the escalating threat posed by Manus Vindictae. Should they succeed in building a large-scale regular force—or if their attacks continue to spread disorder—the proposal urges the Foundation to form its own standing military rather than rely on Zeno. Creius sets forth what he claims is the most efficient approach: recruiting and reorganizing both human and arcanist soldiers already at the front.

This is madness. Does he intend to make the Foundation a rival to every government on earth—an entity viewed with still deeper suspicion? Creius has always been radical, but war elevates such voices. He shows no concern for how the world might react, arguing instead that "we live in an age the Storm could erase at any moment, so we are not obliged to heed their protests." Only recently would such words have been unthinkable.

His position is plain: if Manus Vindictae declares open war, governments will have no choice but to align with the Foundation. Yet should we follow his plan, we begin the most perilous of games.

items.text: A False Dawn

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: What's that sound?
Rudolph has set about packing his things. Like many in the trenches, he doesn't have much, but his greatest treasure is a pile of manuscripts and notes.
He lifts his head. A pale look glints behind his glasses.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: What are you standing there for?

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: They're firing again.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: So? Surely you're used to it by now.
The rumble of artillery had become so familiar to them that its return is barely noticed.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: But, isn't there supposed to be a ceasefire? I know it isn't official yet, but there's no point in firing now, is there?

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Ah!
Erich draws in a sharp breath.
A low, ominous whistle follows.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: S**t! Take cover!
All at once, the quiet of the front erupts into fire and fury.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Ugh ... *cough*
The impact of the explosions shakes the trench lines in unyielding waves, the blasts spraying mud and earth in every direction.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Damn it! Has everyone gone mad?! Those old farts! I thought they were supposed to be negotiating peace?

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Why? Why are we fighting again?
Rudolph sprawls out on the ground, trying to find his baggage, which has been scattered in the blast.
Clothes, notes, and cans are buried in loose dirt or carried off in the air.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: No!

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Forget that rubbish! Get inside!
Erich forces the bespectacled soldier into a dugout, then forces himself up to the parapet, peering over with his periscope.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: S**t! S**t! Who in the hell is attacking us?

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: I-I don't know. They're not even wearing blue. They're in all black.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Right. Are they wearing masks? Can they even see through them?

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: *pant* The flank! *pant*
Scouts and messengers dash in every direction, alerting everyone they can reach of the attack.

items.speaker: Spotter
items.text: I don't know who or what they are, *pant* but they're coming from our flank! *pant*

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Damn it all to hell!
A stray bullet shatters his periscope. He tosses the device down with a stream of curses.
He grabs a messenger by the collar.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: All men from the 2nd Company, assemble! Focus fire on enemies in black uniforms!
Their first assault breaks against the renewed defenses.
But the black-clad soldiers seem numb to their losses; they advance in rigid order, stepping over the dead and dying.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Have they lost their minds? They just keep charging right into our gunfire.
Erich steps down from the parapet to relay orders; in every direction he sees his comrades lying wounded.
Only yesterday they had begun to believe their fight was over, but the rattling barrage has shattered their dreams—a new war has begun.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Damn it. What the hell is going on?
Rudolph hasn't reported back. Concerned, Erich begins to search the dim trenches for his friend, only to bump into a striking figure in a white uniform.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Are you the captain of the 2nd Company?
The man speaks with a gravity of command that Erich still has yet to find.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: I am. You're ... with the Foundation?
Creius nods, articulating the battle at hand in an organized manner.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I am Creius, the commander of the Foundation personnel stationed in Montpaix. This is an emergency situation.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Manus Vindictae invaded the safe zone. We neutralized the threat there, but now they're on a mission to kill every human soldier on the front lines.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: Every human soldier? You-You mean, including those on the other side?
He struggles to find sense in the words.
Creius pats the soldier-turned-captain with a firm and steady grip.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: If you're willing to give up this position, follow me.

items.speaker: Erich
items.text: I couldn't give less of a damn about positions, but where are we going?
In a nearby section of trench.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Anyone still standing? Help me clear this bunker!
The field medic arrives in sync with the rest of the Foundation's team.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: Doctor! Doctor! My brother—he's wounded! Please!

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Bring him to me!
The soldier hauls his wounded comrade to the makeshift aid station. The man's leg hangs limp, soaked in dark red blood.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Urgh ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Easy. Put him down here. I'll patch him up. Have you seen any other Foundation personnel?

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: I-I think I saw one—a redhead.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: Good. Go tell him we need medical supplies. They should've brought plenty from Montpaix.

items.speaker: Soldier
items.text: R-Right away!
Next to them, another soldier clutches his thigh, gasping for breath.
Only a moment passes before yet another man is carried in. Marsha makes a brief inspection and returns to the soldier with the injured thigh.

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: I'll stop the bleeding first.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: W-What about him?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: He's dead. Now relax, and try to stay with me.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: He's dead? No!

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Ahhhhh!

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Good heavens! It's over. I'm dead. I'm dead.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Urgh ...

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: No, you're not. Not today, anyway.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Huff ...
His vision blurs—for a moment he thinks he sees a soldier in a gray and blue uniform.

items.speaker: Rudolph
items.text: Is-Is that ...?
Then he blacks out.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Update? Have you located Creius?

items.speaker: Marsha
items.text: He's somewhere in the trench. A soldier spotted him.
The man soon appears before them.
With solemn deference, he nods to the sniper he once pursued.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I didn't expect to run into—

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Save the pleasantries.
The response is blunt.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Marsha made known to me the situation. The Foundation ought to have a sure plan, having requested me to join her.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Speak then, what would you have me do?
Creius adjusts his tone to match.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: The frontline soldiers have little experience fighting enemies with arcane skills.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: If they stay here, it's only a matter of time until they fall to the Manus. I'm going to move them to a safer strategic position.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: However, enemy forces on Hill 299 have us pinned down in the trenches. Manus Vindictae has turned it into an underground fortress, housing an estimated ten thousand troops. They've even—

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: They've even positioned artillery on the hillside. Retreating under that kind of fire would be a death sentence.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Eliminate the threat from Hill 299, then withdraw the troops from the front—this is the Foundation's plan?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: Not the Foundation's plan. Not yet, at least.
An icy restraint condenses in the man's eager eyes.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: This is my course of action.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: How do you intend to do this? Even with an army of a hundred thousand at your command, to take a fortified high ground under artillery fire is no surety.

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: I know. That's why I need your help.
Creius stands solemn and sure, though he knows how absurd his request sounds.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: Such an act is to walk into the valley of the shadow of death. What difference would be made if I lent my aid or withheld it?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: If I recall correctly, Gargoyles are insusceptible to poison gas.

items.speaker: Sentinel
items.text: That's correct. So?

items.speaker: Creius
items.text: So, we may be able to take a subtler approach. Please, come with me; my subordinate will give you the details.
